Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the agenda are on file in the office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. If applicable, materials related to an item on this agenda submitted to the Council after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's office during normal business hours. Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make inquiry concerning the item. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however, to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a presentation shall be limited to up to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council is requested to fill out a green speaker's card available at the entry of the meeting room. The card permits the City to identify persons for purposes of City Council minute preparation. Please see specific agenda sections below for any other requirements related to meeting participation. The City Council, at the direction of the Mayor with concurrence of the Council, may modify the order of items shown on the agenda.
This meeting will be held via videoconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19 and pursuant to the Governor's Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-20 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer's Safer at Home Order (revised March 21, 2020). All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call vote, and the vote will be publicly reported.
HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may
observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. The meeting will not be livestreamed. You may attend the meeting through a computer or telephone:
BY COMPUTER:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/81013446135
Zoom Meeting ID: 810 1344 6135 or
BY TELEPHONE: 1 669 900 9128, Enter Code 810 1344 6135#
HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to submit email correspondence to CityCouncilMeeting@pvestates.org before the meeting begins. The email will be distributed to all councilmembers. Public correspondence submitted electronically via email will be provided to the legislative body, but will not be read aloud at the meeting.
HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: If you would like to address the City Council during the meeting, please email CityCouncilMeeting@pvestates.org by 5:00 p.m. on Tuesday, June 23rd, with (1) your name, (2) the agenda item on which you'd like to speak, and (3) the phone number and/or Zoom name from which you will be calling in to the meeting.

MINUTES
  OF THE JUNE 23, 2020 REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA

A Teleconference meeting of the Palos Verdes Estates City Council meeting via Zoom pursuant
to Executive Order N25-20 issued by Governor Gavin Newsom on March 26, 2020, was called to
order by Mayor McGowan at 6:32 P.M. on June 23, 2020, notice having been given with affidavit
thereto on file. Members of the public were provided with the following information to provide
public input:

  BY COMPUTER:
  https://us02web.zoom.us/j/81013446135

  Zoom Meeting ID: 810 1344 6135 or

  BY TELEPHONE: 1 669 900 9128, Enter Code 810 1344 6135#

NEXT RESOLUTION NO. R20-19

NEXT ORDINANCE NO. O20-745

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE – Waived

PRESENT:

  Mayor McGowan, Mayor Pro Tem Kemps, Councilmembers Davidson, Kao and Lozzi

ABSENT:
  None

ALSO PRESENT:

  City Manager Guglielmo, Assistant City Attorney Cotti, Treasurer Ying, Community
  Development/Public Works Director Rukavina, Planning Manager Rindge, Interim Police
  Chief Dreiling, City Clerk Chaney

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
June 23, 2020
 APPROVAL OF AGENDA

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Davidson, Seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kemps
  to approve the agenda. The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  AYES:  Lozzi, Kao, Davidson, Kemps, McGowan
  NOES:  None

MAYOR’S REPORT – MATTERS OF COMMUNITY INTEREST

Mayor McGowan welcomed City Manager Guglielmo and thanked Community Development/Public
Works Director Rukavina for his contribution as Acting City Manager. He also provided an update
on reopening protocols in coordination with the Department of Public Health and other Beach Cities.

Mayor McGowan introduced Ryan Kramer and presented a Certificate of Recognition for his
achievement of the Eagle Scout Award.

CONSENT AGENDA (ITEMS 1 – 5)

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Davidson, Seconded by Councilmember Kao
  to approve the consent agenda, with corrections to item 1b, June 9, 2020 Regular
  Meeting Minutes. The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  AYES:  Lozzi, Kao, Davidson, Kemps, McGowan
  NOES:  None

PUBLIC COMMENTS FOR ITEMS ON CONSENT AGENDA
The following individual addressed the City Council: Mike Klein for item #5, Traffic Safety
Committee Recommendations

1.  City Council Action Minutes

  Reviewed and approved:

  a.  June 9, 2020 Special Meeting Minutes

  b.  June 9, 2020 Regular Meeting Minutes

2.  Demands of June 23, 2020

  Approved payment of Motions #1 and #2.

  a. Motion #1 – Payroll Warrant of June 12, 2020
  b. Motion #2 – Warrant Register of June 23, 2020

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
June 23, 2020
 3.  Resolution R20-20; Approving the Special Tax Report and Setting the PVE Law

4.  Notice of Election and Request to Consolidate with Statewide General Election and
  Regulations for Candidate Statements

  Adopted Resolution R20-19.

5.  Traffic Safety Committee Recommendations

  Reviewed and approved the Traffic Safety Committee’s recommendations.

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

The following individuals addressed the City Council: Danny Stender, Desiree Myers, Merlin David

CEREMONIAL MATTERS - None

ORDINANCE/PUBLIC HEARING(S)

6.  Introduction on First Reading of Ordinance No. O20-745 Amending Section 2.24.120 of
  Chapter 2.24 of Title 2 of the Palos Verdes Estates Municipal Code Relating to the
  Investment Policy Advisory Committee

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Kao, Seconded by Councilmember Lozzi to
  Introduce upon first reading Ordinance No. O20-745 Amending Section 2.24.120 of Chapter

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
June 23, 2020
 8.  Update and Discussion of the Activities of the Pension Ad Hoc Committee and the Police

  receive updates from the Ad Hoc Committees on a quarterly basis, or more frequently as

NEW BUSINESS

9.  Award of Maintenance Agreement to Travers Tree Service Inc. for Citywide Tree
  Trimming Services For FY 2020-21

  Recommendation: Award a Tree Trimming Agreement to Travers Tree Service, Inc. to
  perform citywide tree maintenance services through June 30, 2021, in an amount not-to-
  exceed $275,000.

  ACTION: Moved by Mayor Pro Tem Kemps, Seconded by Councilmember Davidson to
  award a Tree Trimming Agreement to Travers Tree Service, Inc. to perform citywide tree
  maintenance services through June 30, 2021, in an amount not-to-exceed $275,000.

  AYES:  Lozzi, Kao, Davidson, Kemps, McGowan
  NOES:  None

10.  Consideration of a Revised and Restated Concession Agreement for Operations of the
  Palos Verdes Beach and Athletic Club and Review and Approval of the
  FY 2020-21 Operating and Capital Budget

  Councilmember Kao recused himself from the meeting during consideration of this item,
  noting that he is currently on the Wait List for the Beach Club.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Lozzi, Seconded by Councilmember Davidson to
  approve the proposed and revised and restated Concession Agreement between the City of
  Palos Verdes Estates and the Palos Verdes Beach and Athletic Foundation and approve the
  FY 2020-21 operating budget and capital budget.

  AYES:  Lozzi, Davidson, Kemps, McGowan
  NOES:  None

STAFF REPORTS

  i.  City Manager's Report

  City Manager Guglielmo reported.

  a. State of the Police Department – Oral Report

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
June 23, 2020
   Interim Police Chief Dreiling reported.

MAYOR & CITY COUNCILMEMBERS' REPORTS

Councilmember Davidson requested future agenda items for a grant writer, the Mirlo Gate House,
Term Limits for City Council, and a Golf Tournament Fundraiser for the City.

Councilmember Lozzi welcomed City Manager Guglielmo, requested that the Council revisit goal
setting, and requested future agenda items for a meeting regarding the Fire Department Contract, a
review of the traffic safety plan for Malaga Cove, and a pension reform strategy.

Councilmember Kao welcomed City Manager Guglielmo, requested that the Traffic Safety turn circle
study be revisited, congratulated this year’s Graduates and bid farewell to John Chanfreau of the Palos
Verdes Tennis Club.

Community Development/Public Works Director Rukavina noted that the City has applied for a grant
through the South Bay Cities Council of Governments that would fund the next phase of the Traffic
Safety study that Councilmembers Lozzi and Kao mentioned.

Mayor Pro Tem Kemps mentioned Southern California Edison’s green energy program and requested
that the City Manager communicate information to the public about opting in to the program. He
provided his comments regarding the Budget and Pension Liabilities, requesting that Budget
documents in the future reflect the City’s financial position, and requested a future agenda item for
the City to review it’s website for Transparency.

Mayor McGowan asked that the Council adjourn the meeting in memory of Mayor Pro Tem Kemp’s
mother.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Davidson, Seconded by Councilmember Kao to
  adjourn the meeting at 8:29 p.m.

  AYES:  Lozzi, Kao, Davidson, Kemps, McGowan
  NOES:  None

RESPECTFULLY SUBMITTED,

___________________________________
Kylynn Chaney, City Clerk

  APPROVED:

  ___________________________________
  David McGowan, Mayor
